title: GraffitiWear — School Community Apparel
jpTitle: GraffitiWear — スクールコミュニティアパレル
organization: Japanese Weekend School of New York (JWSNY)

summary.en: Designed a graffiti-inspired apparel collection for the Japanese Weekend School of New York, blending NYC street-art aesthetics with Japanese school heritage through hand-drawn typography and symbolic illustration. Led execution through an on-campus pop-up store launch; over 50% of students, faculty and parents adopted the merchandise.
summary.jp: ニューヨーク日本語学校向けのアパレルを作った。NY のストリートアートと日本の校風を重ねた。学内のポップアップストアまで主導し、生徒・教職員・保護者の半数以上が身につけた。

mine: Designed apparel using bold hand-drawn typography and symbolic illustrations representing learning, friendship and cultural identity
Drew a graffiti-inspired aesthetic from NYC street-art traditions while honoring Japanese heritage
Led the on-campus pop-up store experience, turning the launch into a community celebration
team: School Parents Association — credited on the page without individual task breakdown

label.en: adoption among students, faculty and parents

narrative.problem: JWSNY lacked a unified community identity that could bridge its educational mission with the vibrant street culture of New York City.

_notes: Client is a school parents association; engagement not explicitly labeled volunteer or freelance on the page, so recorded as unstated.
